Commentary.Commentary: What was that? It seemed as if Bangladesh simply did not turn up. There was no intent in scoring and only  three batters reached double figures. Sri Lanka were tight in the field and did not allow the Bangladeshis to get away at all. Shashikala Siriwardene, in her final game, finished with 4 wickets. But Dilhari, Prabodhani and Kulasuriya choked the opposition. This should be an easy chase. Stay tuned.

Shashikala Siriwardene is down for a chat with Alan Wilkins. On being asked about today's performance, Shashikala says that she is feeling very happy as she could contribute in he final game for her team. On being emotional, Siriwardene admits she was, at the start, but soon got over it. Thanks both teams for giving her the respect. On her retirement decision, Shashikala says that she has played cricket for 17 years, which is nearly 75 percent of her life. States that there are personal priorities in her life and she is getting old. Smiles and says that she wished to have at least one 5-fer in her career but is happy with the same.

OUT! A run out to end a bizarre innings. Full and outside off, Salma drives this through the covers. The batters should have been running for two and Sultana rightly comes back for the second. But, for some reason, Khatun is not even interested. Both batters are at the bowler's end. The fielder throws it to the bowler who fires it to the keeper. The bails are taken off and BANGLADESH FINISH ON 91/8.
Flicks this through mid-wicket for one more.
Full on middle, pushed straight to mid on.
FOUR! Full and outside off, Salma comes down the track and swings it over mid-wicket. Long on gets across to her right and dives but the ball goes through.
Full and outside off, swept through square leg for a run.
DROPPED! Landed outside off, Nigar looks to run it down to third man but hits it straight into the gloves of the keeper. However, the stumper drops it and the ball goes through. A single taken.
Full and around off, swept off the gloves through fine leg for one. 4-0-16-4 for Siriwardene in her final match. Take a bow.
OUT! CAUGHT! Wicket number 4 for Shashikala! Full and outside off, Fahima comes down the track and looks to go big but gets a top edge. Sugandika Kumari takes another catch.
Outside off, chopped down to point for a run.
Full and around off again, the sweep is employed but a top edge results. A single taken towards deep mid-wicket.
Full and around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.

OUT! CAUGHT! Third wicket for Siriwardene. Full and outside off, Moni comes down the track and looks to go over mid off but mistimes it pretty badly. Sugandika Kumari runs back and takes a simple catch.

MISFIELD, FOUR! A rare poor effort in the field today. A length ball, Sultana punches it down the ground. Mid off gets to it but fumbles. The ball goes behind and the fielder recovers, only to fumble again while trying to retrieve the ball. 10 from the over.
FOUR! BLAST! A short ball, around off, Nigar comes down the track and hammers it over mid off for a boundary!
Oops... nearly a return catch! A short ball, outside off, NS looks to pull but the ball barely comes off the surface. Takes the toe end back to the bowler but lands short.
A length ball, outside off, swung towards deep mid-wicket for just a run.
Full and wide outside off, Nigar throws her bat at it and gets a thick outside edge which flies over point. A single taken.
A length ball, outside off, Sultana looks to cut but misses. Beaten by pace.
Achini Kulasuriya returns. 2-0-9-2 so far.
Full and outside off, Moni runs it down to short third man and sets off for a single but is sent back.
Tossed up outside off, driven gloriously, coming down the track but straight to short extra cover.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
Down the leg side, tickled fine for a single.
Comes down the track and sweeps it through mid-wicket. Good effort in the deep, ensures that it is just a couple.
Full and around off, driven back to the bowler.
Comes down the track and drives it down the ground but short extra cover dives and prevents any run. That is the end of Kavisha Dilhari. 4-0-13-1.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Comes down the track but is not to the pitch of the ball. Defends.
Full and outside off, pretty wide, driven through the covers for a single.
This time she hangs back and looks to tap and run towards point but the fielder comes in pretty quickly.
Full and outside off, Moni comes down the track and drives it straight to short extra cover.
Short, stays low, pulled to deep mid-wicket for one more.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
Comes down the track and hacks it through mid-wicket. Just a single.
Full on middle, pushed towards the bowler.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a single.
The captain now. Here comes Chamari Atapattu. A bit late today.
Works this through mid-wicket for a run.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Flicks this through the leg side for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover for a quick single. The bowler herself goes after it, picks the ball, turns and has a shy at the bowler's end. Misses, but the batter was well in.
Outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Ritu Moni walks in next at number 7, replacing Rumana.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another wicket for the woman in her final T20I. Full and around off, Rumana gets down and looks to sweep but gets a top edge which goes straight to short fine leg. Udeshika Prabodhani makes no mistake. Half the side is down.
Landed outside off, driven back to Shashikala.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Landed outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, Rumana looks to run it down to third man but misses.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Shashikala Siriwardene is back on. 2-0-11-1 so far.
Rumana Ahmed walks in at number 6, replacing Fargana.

OUT! LBW! Given Fargana's confidence, one felt that there was bat. But nope. Full and in line of the stumps, Fargana got down to sweep but missed. She was hit flush on the pads and at that moment itself, one felt it was plumb. Hoque immediately took the review though. No spike on the Ultra Edge. Ball Tracker shows it to be spinning down the leg side but just about clipping the outer half of leg stump. Not a bad review. It is retained but the batter is gone. A decent 31-run stand has been broken.

Fargana has been adjudged LBW! She takes the review immediately. Was there bat? Not according to the replays or Ultra Edge. Ball Tracker shows it to be clipping leg stump, so the decision stays as it is.
WIDE. Full and around off, Sultana looks to flick but the ball spins past the pad and beats the keeper. Wide signalled as the batters take a single.
FOUR! Glorious shot. Full and outside off, Sultana comes down the track and lofts it with ease over extra cover.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Comes down the track and slices this straight to point. Lands short.
Full and outside off, slogged past a diving short mid-wicket for a single towards long on. 50 UP FOR BANGLADESH. 50 balls left.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Full and around off, watchfully pressed forward for a single. 10 from the over.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
WIDE. Full and down the leg side, sweep shot missed.
FOUR! Delightful shot. Full and outside off, Nigar gets her dancing shoes on, reaches the pitch of the ball and lofts it inside out over cover.
Full and around middle, eased down to long on for one.
Outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
Full on middle, pushed through mid on for a single.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler. 39/3 at the halfway stage.
Low, dipping full toss, swept through square leg for a run.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full and around off, Sultana comes down the track and drives it towards mid off for a quick single.
Full and outside off, swept powerfully but straight to square leg.
Full and around middle, watchfully defended.
Kavisha Dilhari into the attack as well.
This is pushed down to wide long on for one more.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
Fuller, just outside off, well defended.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Landed outside off, Fargana looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto her pads.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Sugandika Kumari to bowl now.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for one.
FOUR! BLAST! A short ball, on middle, Fargana pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary!
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
Down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, played towards point. There is a bit of a mix-up but all is well in the end.
Full and outside off, pushed towards third man for a run. Prabodhani is done, with 4 overs on the trot. 4-0-13-0.
Full on middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.

NOT OUT. Review gone. Full and outside off, angling away, Nigar reaches out to push but misses. The bowler and keeper get excited but the umpire is unmoved. There is a lot of chitchat and eventually, the review is taken. Ultra Edge shows nothing.
Is that another wicket? Prabodhani is confident that Nigar has nicked this. Atapattu takes the review. Nothing on the Ultra Edge.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Outside off, another play and a miss.
Full and outside off, Sultana looks to push but misses.
A length ball, outside off, Hoque looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto her pads. 26/3 in the Powerplay. Sensational start by Sri Lanka!

WIDE. A short ball, down the leg side, Fargana looks to pull but misses. The bowler thinks there is glove involved and wants the review. The captain comes in but then is advised not to take the review. Ultra Edge detects nothing.
Fargana Hoque walks in at number 5, on the final ball of the Powerplay.

OUT! LBW! Three down in the Powerplay! Kulasuriya has two in the over. A length ball, outside off, Ayasha looks to defend but the ball comes back in off the seam and hits her on the pads. Kulasuriya appeals, the umpire takes her time and eventually raises her finger. Rahman is not too sure. She walks down the pitch, has a long chat with Sultana and then signals for the review. But she is TIMED OUT. Ball Tracker shows that it would have been umpire's call on hitting the stumps. Clipping the bails.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
On a length outside off, Sultana feels for it but misses.
Nigar Sultana walks in now.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Kulasuriya strikes with her first ball. Not her best but she will take it. Short and wide outside off, there to be hit and Sanjida slashes hard. But there is no foot movement and the result is a thin outside edge. The ball dies on its way to the keeper but Anushka Sanjeewani dives low and to her right to snaffles it.
Achini Kulasuriya to bowl the final over of the Powerplay.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Another single taken down leg.
Works this down the leg side for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed through mid off for one.
Full and down the leg side, flicked through fine leg. Harshitha Madavi gets across from deep backward square leg and dives, stopping the ball. Two runs taken.
On middle, punched towards mid on for a quick single.
Outside off, punched towards mid on for a quick single. 11 from the over.

MISSES THE STUMPS! Lot of turn. Full and outside off, Islam gets across, looks to sweep but misses this time. The ball spins past the leg stump and the blinded keeper cannot do much. The ball goes between her legs. Good stop by short fine leg.

FOUR! Excellent batting. Full and in line of the stumps, a bit quicker as well, Sanjida again gets across and sweeps it powerfully through square leg. There is a fielder in the deep who runs barely 10 paces to her right but the ball races past her!
Outside off, no pace to work with, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Terrific shot. Full and outside off, Sanjida reaches out and sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary!
Full on middle, nicely played down the ground to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Down the leg side, played straight to short mid-wicket.
Outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Full and around middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
On middle, driven straight to mid on.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Sanjida Islam walks in at number 3, replacing Murshida Khatun.

OUT! CAUGHT! The accuracy of Siriwardene is terrific. Full and around off, Murshida looks to play the slog sweep but gets a massive top edge. The ball is high in the air and Hasini Perera from first slip calls for it. She runs towards leg slip, loses it in the air as the ball swirls but then manages to take it in the end with a dive. Early strike then.
Full and around off, Ayasha gets across and looks to flick but misses. The ball goes off her pads towards fine leg and a leg bye is taken.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full on middle and leg, flicked wide of mid on for a single.
Shashikala Siriwardene to bowl from the other end.
Outside off, driven sweetly through the covers but just a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

This does not look good at all. Umesha Thimashini is clutching her left shoulder and the physio is out in the middle. The hand is barely moving. This is looking really, really bad. And THIMASHINI IS GOING OFF.

Quick single but what has happened here? Umesha Thimashini is on the ground, yelping in pain. Ayasha pushed this down the ground and called for a quick single. Thimashini charged across from mid off and looked to dive but in the process, lost her balance and almost did a somersault. Deadly scenes.

DIRECT HIT WOULD HAVE BEEN CURTAINS! Full on middle, Murshida pushes it towards mid on and makes a late call for the single. The fielder charges onto the ball, has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Khatun would have been gone.
On middle, pushed straight to mid on.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.

The national anthems are done and the players take their positions on the field. Ayasha Rahman and Murshida Khatun are the Bangladesh openers. Udeshika Prabodhani, left-arm fast medium, to start off proceedings against Khatun. Here we go...
Time for the national anthems. Bangladesh's first.
PITCH REPORT - Anjum Chopra near the deck states that this is a fresh pitch. Believes that it will be a very good one for batting.

Sri Lanka Women (Playing XI) - Chamari Atapattu (C), Umesha Thimashini, Hasini Perera, Harshitha Madavi, Anushka Sanjeewani (WK), Shashikala Siriwardene, Nilakshi de Silva, Kavisha Dilhari, Sugandika Kumari (IN FOR HANSIMA KARUNARATNE), Udeshika Prabodhani and Achini Kulasuriya (IN FOR SATHYA SANDEEPANI).

Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Murshida Khatun, Ayasha Rahman, Sanjida Islam (IN FOR SOBHANA MOSTARY), Nigar Sultana (WK), Fargana Hoque, Rumana Ahmed, Ritu Moni, Fahima Khatun, Salma Khatun (C), Panna Ghosh and Nahida Akter (IN FOR JAHANARA ALAM).

Sri Lankan skipper, Chamari Atapattu, says that she was anyway looking to bowl first, so is happy. States that she is very confident about her bowling unit, especially Shashikala Siriwardene. Informs that there are two changes to the side, with Achini Kulasuriya and Sugandika Kumari coming in. Agrees that this is a very big game for them and wants to beat Bangladesh and go back home with a win.

Bangladesh captain, Salma Khatun says that the weather and wicket, both are good, hence the reason to bat first. Informs that there are two changes. Remembers that Jahanara Alam is sitting out and Nahida Akter comes in her place, but forgets the other change. Says that this is their last game and wants to sign off with a win.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. Sri Lanka are the home team, so Chamari Atapattu will flip the coin. Heads is the call from Salma Khatun and it is a head. BANGLADESH WILL BAT FIRST.

It is quarter-finals day! Well, not in entirety. The tournament is reaching its dying stages and all eyes would be on the Australia-New Zealand encounter, to decide who would be the second semi-finalist, joining India. But first up, is a dead rubber, between two Asian sides - Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. Both have been average in this tournament and would love to end it with a win, or at least bow out with some fight. Hello and a warm welcome to Match 17 from the Junction Oval in Melbourne.
